## In-Depth LinkedIn Optimization With Marketing Management Techniques

[[This paper applies marketing management tools to my LinkedIn profile and aims it at freight transportation, the segment that produced 60.88% of Canadian freight and logistics revenue in 2025 (Mordor Intelligence, 2026). I want to work in that field in Metro Vancouver. The industry data and the 10 local job postings reviewed here decide how I present my two years as a logistics coordinator at GLT Logistics and my current stockroom role at Garage Clothing to recruiters and operations managers.]]

[[This project looks at logistics in Canada, mainly freight transportation and the digital services that firms use to book and coordinate shipments. Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (2018) defines logistics as the planning, implementation, and control of the movement and storage of goods, services, and related information, which in daily business links suppliers, plants, warehouses, carriers, and customers. Moving the freight is only part of the job.]] Distribution also breaks down when inventory records are wrong, when orders wait to be processed, or when the carrier and the customer are working from different information.

The industry is closely tied to the domestic economy and to international trade, as transportation and warehousing contributed CAD 96.5 billion, or 4.3% of national GDP, in 2024 (Transport Canada, 2025b). In that same year Canada’s international merchandise trade reached approximately CAD 1.55 trillion, of which, measured by value, road transportation carried 46%, marine transport 21.1%, air 11.6%, and rail 10.5%, so the first set of figures describes the output of the transportation and warehousing sector, whereas the second describes the value of the merchandise flows that the network moves.

Mordor Intelligence (2026) estimates that freight transportation accounted for 60.88% of the Canadian freight and logistics market in 2025, and that share, combined with the growing use of digital freight marketplaces, makes this field a reasonable starting point for examining employers and the qualifications they look for. Freightera, a Vancouver-based business-to- business platform on which shippers compare and book freight, offers a useful example of this type of service (Freightera, n.d.-a).

Ken Research (n.d.) estimates that the market increased from USD 97 billion in 2021 to USD 112 billion in 2025, a cumulative gain of approximately 15.5%, and more than half of that USD 15 billion increase came in 2022 alone, since annual growth stayed below 3% from 2023 onward.
Estimated Market Value of the Canadian Logistics Industry, 2021–2025

Freight demand came back once the first COVID-19 restrictions eased, and Transport Canada (2022) recorded more port container traffic and more truck crossings than in 2020. [[The network stayed fragile, though. Containers were scarce, overseas sailings ran late, and wildfires and severe flooding in British Columbia cut key routes, so a container travelling from Shanghai to Toronto through West Coast ports took 34.5 days on average that year, against 25.9 days in 2019 (Transport Canada, 2026).]]

[[In 2022 the market estimate rose to USD 105 billion, the largest annual gain of the period (Ken Research, n.d.). Disruption in world supply markets raised export demand for Canadian commodities, while imported goods kept terminals and inland connections under pressure]] (Transport Canada, 2023), and the average container journey from Shanghai to Toronto reached 39.9 days, the longest of the five years (Transport Canada, 2026). Freight rates and tight capacity explain part of the USD 8 billion increase, so the higher value does not mean that more goods moved or that service improved.
## 2023: Weaker Goods Demand and Labour Disruption

Growth slowed to 2.9% in 2023 as inflation, higher financing costs, and softer spending reduced demand for some imported and industrial goods (Ken Research, n.d.; Transport Canada, 2024). The July labour dispute at British Columbia ports was especially disruptive, since merchandise imports cleared through those ports fell 18.5% relative to June and exports departing them fell 23.0%, according to figures that Statistics Canada (2023) did not seasonally adjust, and although transit from Shanghai to Toronto improved to 35.0 days, part of that relief reflected the reduced congestion that came as demand eased (Transport Canada, 2026).

The market estimate reached USD 111 billion in 2024, an increase of 2.8% (Ken Research, n.d.), while freight volumes recovered in several transport modes with results that varied across Canadian gateways, as Transport Canada (2025a) reported higher container activity at major ports alongside continued interruptions from labour disputes and extreme weather. Online retail, for its part, remained a meaningful source of distribution demand, since Statistics Canada (2026a) measured CAD 73.7 billion in e-commerce operating revenue for 2024, a figure 9.0% above that of 2023.

Although the market estimate edged up just 0.9% in 2025, to USD 112 billion (Ken Research, n.d.), the geography of freight changed considerably, as Transport Canada (2026) found that Canadian merchandise exports to the United States fell about 5% while exports to other markets climbed roughly 16%. Truck entries into Canada decreased by about 5% and U.S.- linked rail freight weakened, but marine gateways gained from overseas trade, with the Port of Vancouver handling a record 170.4 million metric tonnes, 8% more than in 2024, and with container transit from Shanghai to Toronto improving to 33.3 days, although it remained noticeably slower than in 2019 (Transport Canada, 2026).

Over these five years, a rebound in demand first exceeded the practical capacity of parts of the network, after which shipping conditions normalized, freight activity weakened on some routes, and service reliability gradually improved, until by 2025 trade policy was changing the geography of freight demand, putting transborder trucking under pressure while ocean-oriented corridors gained business. [[With Shanghai–Toronto transit moving between 39.9 days in 2022 and 33.3 days in 2025, employers needed people who could track a container, warn the customer early, and find another route when a corridor slowed down.]]

[[Mordor Intelligence (2026) puts the freight and logistics market at USD 111.66 billion in 2025 and USD 116.63 billion in 2026, and expects USD 145.05 billion by 2031, a compound annual growth rate of 4.45%.]]
Note. Data from Mordor Intelligence (2026). Values for 2027–2030 are interpolated at the forecast’s implied compound annual growth rate of 4.45%.

Conditions during 2026 help explain both the opportunity and the risk contained in that projection, since real GDP increased 0.8% in the second quarter, supported by exports, spending, and investment (Statistics Canada, 2026b), while the Bank of Canada (2026) projects 1.0% real GDP growth for the year and warns of persistent energy-price pressures and uncertainty over U.S. trade policy. The Bank’s October report also expects inflation of 2.9% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027, which for road carriers means higher fuel and input costs and thinner margins, even if the nominal value of logistics services keeps rising.

Online shopping should keep demand high for fulfilment, warehousing, and parcel delivery. Mordor Intelligence (2026) expects courier, express, and parcel services to grow faster than the market as a whole, in line with the rise in online retail documented by Statistics Canada (2026a). [[Trade diversification helps ports, rail, and intermodal carriers, above all when exporters look for routes that do not run through the United States (Transport Canada, 2026).]]

[[Digital tools let companies plan routes, flag exceptions, and coordinate shipments, but they pay off only when they fit into daily work and the staff know how to use them. Freightera already lets shippers compare carriers and manage documents online (Freightera, n.d.-a). Emissions also enter the decision, since transport produced about 22% of Canada’s greenhouse gas emissions in 2024, counting passenger and freight activity (Transport Canada, 2026). Fuel efficiency, better use of network capacity, and lower-emission modes may soon weigh as much as price and service when a customer chooses a logistics provider.]]

[[Taken together, the figures point to moderate growth. Mordor’s 4.45% annual rate depends on demand for specialized, data-driven services, while labour availability, energy costs, climate-related disruption, and North American trade conditions could all slow it down.]]

## Competencies in Metro Vancouver Job Advertisements

[[I then tested the choice on the local market. The sample has 10 advertisements from Vancouver, North Vancouver, Richmond, Surrey, and Burnaby, three from LinkedIn and seven from employer, staffing-firm, or local job-board sites.]] Six are freight or logistics jobs and four are inventory or planning jobs. A competency counted once per posting if it showed up as a requirement, an asset, or a stated duty.

All 10 advertisements describe communication with customers, carriers, colleagues, or other stakeholders, nine mention Excel or Microsoft Office, and nine refer to solving problems or resolving exceptions, while eight include operational records and eight name an operating system such as ERP, TMS, WMS, or MRP. Inventory or stock control appears in seven postings, and shipment scheduling or tracking and reporting or analysis appear in six postings each, three of which (C, E, and J) require both, so the two counts only partly overlap, given that a shipment coordinator needs to keep freight visible, whereas an inventory coordinator is more likely to work with counts, discrepancies, and performance reports.

To them, I am a logistics coordinator with an industrial engineering background who keeps freight and stock visible, because I provided freight-status updates at GLT Logistics, coordinate stock movement and replenishment at Garage Clothing, and completed postgraduate studies in data analytics at Douglas College.]]
## Marketing Mix: The 4Ps of Personal Branding

[[Following Gomez Albrecht et al. (2023), I adapted the four Ps to a personal brand. Product is the experience I offer, Price is the pay range I can defend, Place covers the channels where employers will find me, and Promotion is the way I show my work and take part in conversations. Table 8 records the decision for each one.]]

[[My offer combines two years of freight coordination at GLT Logistics, stockroom operations at Garage Clothing, and earlier work in purchasing, planning, and operational indicators at Colombina and Veplast. Having worked on both sides of a shipment, I can speak to the customer who is waiting for freight and to the internal steps of receiving and replenishing stock. The profile will describe those duties and add one work sample that shows how I analyze data.]]

The market analysis gave me the criteria for reviewing my profile, namely that a recruiter should be able to recognize the role I am targeting and that an operations manager should be able to see how my experience relates to the work, so I began with LinkedIn’s guidance on completing a profile and then compared my existing wording with the skills and duties found in the local advertisements.

LinkedIn recommends a recognizable professional photo, a background image, an About section that explains the professional story, and Experience and Skills sections that reflect career goals (LinkedIn, n.d.-a). For the photo, that means good light, a plain background, and a crop that keeps my face clear on a phone screen, while the banner can use the space next to the portrait to name my field. [[Both should be checked on a laptop and on a phone.]]

## Profile Assessment With ChatGPT and Resume Worded

[[I used ChatGPT (OpenAI, 2026) to compare my headline, About, Experience, and Skills sections with the duties in the local advertisements. I asked it to sort the requirements into those my profile already supports, those that are present but hard to find, and those that need more evidence. According to the comparison, my GLT and Garage entries already cover freight communication, stock movement, and shipment processing. The gap was in where that evidence]] appeared. [[My headline was broad, my About section did not connect the two jobs, and some relevant skills were scattered across duplicate entries.]]

[[The comparison also flagged claims I need to check. Microsoft Office is listed, but I still have to confirm which Excel functions I can use on my own. SAP ERP is listed too, while the advertisements name several other systems. I will add TMS, WMS, CargoWise, or advanced Excel only when I can show where I used them, since a term missing from my profile is not automatically a weakness. Appendix C contains my prompt and explains how I reviewed the output.]]

[[I will run Resume Worded’s LinkedIn Review (Resume Worded, n.d.) before and after the changes, following the steps in Appendix C. Its scores and section feedback can then be compared with the ChatGPT results and with the requirements in Table 5.]]

[[I recorded the first-day values on November 11, 2026. The dashboard showed 1,085 followers, no post impressions in the seven-day window, three profile viewers over 90 days, and six search appearances between October 27 and November 2, while the profile itself read “500+ connections.” These numbers do not measure the same thing. Search appearances count how often I turn up in searches, profile views count the people who opened the profile, and impressions count how often my content was seen (LinkedIn, n.d.-b, n.d.-e).]]

[[Right now my profile uses Industrial Engineering, Data Analytics, Logistics, Freight Transportation, Inventory Management, SAP ERP, Microsoft Office, and Power BI as search terms, and Logistics Coordinator appears in the banner. In the revised profile each term goes to the section that backs it up, with “Logistics Coordinator” in my headline and GLT title, freight status updates in my About section and GLT description, and inventory management and]] replenishment under Garage, while reporting and SAP ERP remain where I can explain their use. [[Should my account show who searched for me or which terms they used, I will copy that information as it appears and keep it apart from my own keyword list, which only covers the text I wrote.]]

[[These measures will decide what I adjust next. If search appearances rise above the six of the first week while profile views stay near three, I will revisit how well my headline and location match the target jobs. If views go up without new relevant connections or conversations, I will check whether my Experience and Featured sections give a reader a reason to contact me. A post with impressions but few reactions or comments will make me rethink its topic, opening, and question before I write the next one. Followers and connections show how my network changes, and I will also look at whether the new people work in the areas I selected.]]
